title: Copperline Insurance — Private Deploy capacity, architecture Q&A, and Terraform module handoff
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the proposed capacity sizing, architecture questions & answers, and a first-cut Terraform module handoff plan for Copperline Insurance's private deployment (VPC + on-prem colocation hybrid). It is intended for the rollout engineering team and the customer infra leads.

Context / customer goals (summary):
- Copperline wants a private inference endpoint for their claim-processing assistant. All inference traffic must originate from their VPC or over a private MPLS link.
- Target latency: p95 < 220ms for 64-token completions, expected average token length ~80.
- Expected steady-state traffic: 12 qps average with 95th percentile bursts to 40 qps during business hours.
- Data residency: primary in us-east-1, with a DR site in eu-west-1 for critical workflows.
- Compliance: SOC2 + early PCI-Scope considerations (cardholder data never sent to Redwood).
- Ops requirement: Blue/green upgrades with ability to rollback model binary and runtime versions.

High-level architecture we propose (concept):
- Customer VPC (Copperline) -> Transit gateway / PrivateLink -> Redwood Private control plane (customer-managed) for metadata and telemetry only (no PII).
- Inference runtime in a colocated rack (customer-owned colo) in us-east region (primary), with an optional warm standby cluster in eu-west (DR).
- Edge NAT/egress via Copperline perimeter; Redwood runtime connects outbound to control plane over mutual TLS.
- Local KMS integration: customer KMS accessible from colo (via HSM appliance or cloud KMS peering).
- Model artifacts mirrored to local object storage (S3-compatible minio in colo) under a read-only practice for runtime.

Sizing assumptions (explicit) — please review and confirm with Copperline infra: 
- Inference model: 7B dense-ish transformer, quantized to int8 in our runtime benchmarks.
- Token throughput: avg 80 tokens/request, 12 qps steady = 960 tokens/s steady; 40 qps bursts = 3200 tokens/s.
- Per-GPU throughput (estimate, int8): ~600 tokens/s for 7B on an A10G-like card under our batcher with target latency p95 ~200ms (this figure depends on sequence length/batching).
- Effective GPUs required (math): steady 960 / 600 = 1.6 -> 2 GPUs; burst headroom 3200 / 600 = 5.3 -> 6 GPUs for burst capacity if colocated with instant scaling.
- Operational choice: provision 6 GPUs across 3 hosts (2 GPUs/host) to tolerate 1 host failure and still handle ~4 GPUs capacity (~2400 tokens/s) and accept graceful degradation for bursts.
- Storage: 1TB NVMe per host for model KV + local caches.
- Network: 25Gbps per host recommended to avoid host-level egress bottlenecks (KV cache transfers, model pull).
- Memory: 384GB RAM per host to accommodate OS, container runtime, and large KV cache for batching.
- Kubernetes: small k8s cluster using node pools for inference worker (GPU nodes) and control-plane (private management nodes).

Operational tradeoffs we considered: 
- Option A: Provision 6 GPUs on-prem (lowest cross-network variance, full privacy).
- Option B: 4 GPUs on-prem + burst to Redwood Dedicated in us-east via PrivateLink (saves colo capital, slightly higher variability).
- Recommendation: start with Option B in pilot for cost flexibility, then evaluate moving to Option A in steady state if privacy/cost justify.

Terraform module strategy (handoff notes for infra team):
- Modules to add under "private-deploy-modules":
  - copperline-networking: constructs: vpc, subnets, route tables, private endpoint for control-plane, security groups, NACLs.
  - copperline-k8s-cluster: EKS/managed k8s bootstrap module (or kubeadm for colo), node pools (gpu, infra), taints/tolerations.
  - copperline-gpu-hosts: module that standardizes instance type, attached NVMe, teardown protection, and GPU driver bootstrapping.
  - artifacts-sync: bucket lifecycle + replication config for model artifacts (S3-compatible target).
  - kms-integration: constructs for customer KMS wiring and minimal IAM permissions (read-only for runtime).
  - private-link-proxy: resources to create PrivateLink endpoints and connection with Redwood control plane.
- Remote state: use S3 backend (customer-owned S3 in their acct) + DynamoDB for state locking. For colo-only customers without S3, fallback to an internal state bucket in the customer's central account; explicit manual steps in README.
- Secrets: do not store KMS keys in TF state. Use provided secrets manager references (customer HashiVault, or native cloud KMS secret references).
- Versioning: tag modules with semver. Initial handoff version: v0.1.0. Include acceptance tests as terraform-validate + simple apply in non-prod tenant.

Terraform variables & minimal example (text snippet):
- variables to expose: region, vpc_cidr, allocator_subnets, gpu_node_count, gpu_instance_profile, control_plane_endpoint, kms_key_arn, model_artifact_url, remote_state_bucket
- Example usage (pseudocode):
  module "copperline-network" {
    source = "git::github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-modules//copperline-networking?ref=v0.1.0"
    region = "us-east-1"
    vpc_cidr = "10.20.0.0/16"
  }

Preflight checklist for Copperline infra (to validate before runbook applies):
- [ ] PrivateLink or TGW peering approved by network team (ticket JIRA-CI-7462).
- [ ] KMS policy allowed to be called from colocated hosts; provide key ARN and demo access.
- [ ] Rack power and cooling confirmed for 3 hosts with GPUs (2x GPU per host).
- [ ] BGP/MPLS or direct connect schedule for colo to cloud control-plane egress if required.
- [ ] DNS delegation for model artifact endpoints or signed URL strategy approved.

Upgrade & rollback plan (runtime + model):
- Canary path: route 5% traffic to new model runtime pool for 60 minutes. Metrics to watch: p95 latency, error rate, token dropout.
- If regressions > 5% in metrics, auto rollback to previous deployment.
- Terraform plan/apply sequence for upgrades:
  1) Prepare new AMI/container image in staging.
  2) Update module version in tfvars and run terraform plan in staging account.
  3) Apply to staging and run synthetic load test.
  4) Create new k8s nodepool with new runtime image, cordon/drain old nodes incrementally.
  5) If rollback required, scale back nodepool and revert module/version.

Open questions / decisions for the customer (action items):
- Do they prefer colo-owned k8s (kubeadm) or managed k8s (EKS-on-prem partners)?
- Are strict PCI controls required on the runtime host (do we need PCI-hardened images)?
- Preferred artifact sync strategy: push (Redwood->minio) vs. pull (runtime fetches from Redwood artifact service)?
- DR RPO target: acceptable warm-up time for failover model cache?

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Network latency variability: mitigate with local artifact mirror + larger KV cache and smaller batch window.
- GPU driver compatibility on commodity hosts: mitigate with baked AMI images and preflight checklist.
- Terraform drift between Copperline changes and module updates: mitigate with scheduled drift detection (monthly) and automated tf plan alerts.

Next steps / immediate owners:
- Riley Nguyen (Redwood): produce v0.1 TF module PR for copperline-networking and copperline-gpu-hosts (due 2025-02-14).
- Mateo Alvarez (Redwood): run lab benchmark on 7B quantized model for exact tokens/s on target host spec and report numbers (due 2025-02-07).
- Copperline infra lead (TBD): confirm rack power/cooling and provide KMS ARN (due 2025-02-10).

Notes to self / loose items: 
- Keep a short-runbook for manual model rollback in case canary detection fails.
- Add quickstart script to modules repo to create non-prod demo in <2 hours for Copperline devs.
- Document expected per-token cost estimate (approx) once Mateo provides measured throughput.

Attachments & references (internal):
- Benchmark log: /mnt/infra/benchmarks/7b-int8-copperline-2025-01-09.log (internal lab)
- Network diagram sketch: CONFLUENCE-1182 (linked_artifacts).

Unresolved/parking-lot questions:
- Confirm if they need split-control-plane (control plane hosted in their acct) vs Redwood-hosted small control plane.
- If customer insists on no outbound connectivity at all, we need alternate artifact delivery (airgap USB transfer or secure on-site sync).

End of draft — please add comments inline in Confluence or open PR feedback on github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-modules/pull/234.
